title: Gateway mTLS + Evidence Orchestration cheatsheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working cheat sheet captures the recommended gateway (edge + internal) mTLS patterns, RBAC v2 signals to emit in audit logs, SIEM export mappings, and small automation recipes for collecting "evidence" when running Private deployments. Intended for solutions engineers doing customer installs and infra engineers who maintain the deployment bundles.

Quick summary (one‑liners):
- Use two-tier mTLS: external gateway (customer-facing) with short-lived certs + internal service mesh mTLS for east‑west.
- RBAC v2: make role assignment events explicit in audit logs (assign, revoke, policy-change, inheritance-eval).
- Evidence automation: scheduled collection of packet-flows, firewall-rule-diffs, cert rotation events, and export to S3/MinIO with tamper-evidence manifest.
- SIEM export: map audit events to common fields (timestamp, principal, action, resource, outcome, request_id, trace_id, evidence_blob).

Architecture notes (ASCII diagram):
[Customer VPC] --- (VPC Peering + Private GW) --- [Edge Gateway (mTLS terminator) ] --- [Internal LB] --- {service-mesh (mTLS)} --- microservices
Key boundaries: external trust boundary ends at Edge Gateway. Internal certs issued by cluster CA and rotated independently.

Gateway mTLS patterns (recommendations):
- TLS profiles: enforce TLS1.3; disable RSA ciphers; require ECDSA or x25519 for key exchange.
- Client auth: Edge Gateway requires client certs for all management/control plane connections. For customer app traffic, support optional client certs + JWT verification as fallback (JWT checked in token-introspect step).
- Cert lifecycle: issue leaf certs TTL=6 hours for ingress-proxies; intermediate CA TTL=90 days; rotate intermediates with staged rollout using canary endpoints.
- Revocation: Prefer short TTLs over CRL checks for scale; publish revocation events to the audit log and SIEM.

VPC & firewall patterns (practical rules to include in install manifest):
- Minimal ingress: allow 443/HTTPS from customer CIDR blocks (or peered VPC CIDRs) only to Edge Gateway IPs.
- Management plane: allow port 8443/9000 only from ops management addresses and from internal subnets; lock down to specific service accounts where cloud NAT is used.
- East-west: only allow intra-cluster CIDR; block cross-az broad CIDR ranges unless explicit.
- Egress: deny by default; allow DNS, NTP, CRL/OCSP endpoints, KMS endpoints, metrics/monitoring endpoints.
- Example cloud firewall rule names (install-standard):
  - allow-edge-https-from-customer
  - allow-management-from-ops
  - allow-metrics-to-observability
  - deny-all-otherwise (high-priority)

RBAC v2 events to emit (audit log guidance):
Emit the following event types with these fields. Each field below is required in the structured audit entry (JSON string in the log):
- role_assignment: {timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, role_id, resource_scope, action: "assign", admin_id, request_id, trace_id, outcome}
- role_revocation: same fields with action: "revoke"
- policy_change: {timestamp, actor, policy_id, delta_summary, affected_roles, request_id, trace_id, outcome}
- policy_evaluation: {timestamp, evaluator_service, principal_id, resource, decision: allow|deny, reason_codes, request_id, trace_id}

Sample audit log schema (include as a single-line JSON example; in practice logs are newline-delimited JSON):
{"ts":"2024-11-08T10:12:07Z","event_type":"role_assignment","principal":{"id":"svc-abc123","type":"service_account"},"role":{"id":"rdw-admin","binding_scope":"project:acme-prod"},"actor":{"id":"user:maya.thompson@redwood.ai","ip":"34.82.11.5"},"request_id":"req-0a1b2c3d","trace_id":"trace-9f8e7d","outcome":"success","evidence_refs":["s3://evidence/acme-prod/2024-11-08/role-assign-req-0a1b2c3d.json"]} 

Evidence automation recipe (ops playbook - compact):
1) Collect baseline: on install, snapshot firewall rules, route tables, VPC flow logs sample for 30s, cert fingerprints, and store to evidence bucket.
2) Periodic (daily): run "evidence-collector" which performs:
   - firewall-diff: compare current firewall rules to baseline and emit delta (JSON).
   - cert-inspector: list all certs (edge + CA) ages and next-rotation window.
   - flow-sampler: collect 1s of VPC flow logs at 30s intervals (sample 10) to capture abnormal connections.
   - audit-grep: pull all RBAC events with outcome!=success for 24h window.
   - sign-manifest: sign the evidence manifest with infra signing key and upload both manifest + tarball to S3/MinIO with retention tags.
3) On security event trigger (SIEM alert): run the on-demand collector which also captures tcpdump at edge for 2 minutes and store encrypted blob + index entry.

Retention & tamper evidence:
- Keep signed manifests with checksums and signer's key fingerprint in logs.
- Track evidence object metadata in DynamoDB/metadata-store: {object_key, sha256, signed_by, created_at, retained_until}.

SIEM export mappings (recommended minimum fields):
- common fields: time, source_host, dest_host, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource, outcome, severity, request_id, trace_id, evidence_blob_url
- Splunk HEC example mapping: send audit JSON as event with "sourcetype":"redwood:audit:rbacv2" and add fields: rb_role, rb_action, rb_scope, outcome
- Elastic ingestion: use ECS-like fields: @timestamp, agent.hostname, user.name, event.action, event.outcome, network.direction, host.ip, url.original (evidence link)

Operational checks (pre-install checklist):
- confirm customer VPC CIDRs and reserved subnets documented
- ops management IP allowlist provided and validated
- customer KMS endpoints reachable from private subnets
- observability endpoints (Prometheus push/grafana) whitelisted if needed

Hardening checklist (minimum controls):
- enforce mtls for all control plane endpoints (no plaintext).
- edge gateway only exposes TLS1.3 and HSTS headers.
- firewall deny-by-default with explicit allow rules.
- short-lived certs for external endpoints, automated rotation pipelines.
- RBAC changes require two-step approval for production scopes (policy-change + role-grant).
- audit logs forwarded to SIEM in near-real-time (<= 2m) and replicated to immutable store.

Troubleshooting quick notes:
- If clients fail TLS handshake: capture edge proxy logs (debug tls) and compare cert fingerprint to CA list.
- If RBAC assignment not taking effect: verify policy_evaluation event; check policy_evaluator container logs and policy delta history.
- If evidence upload fails: check object-store credentials, multipart upload limits, and signing key expiry.

Unresolved / TODOs (open questions for design review):
- Should we standardize on one timestamp format across all components (epoch vs RFC3339)? (bias to RFC3339)
- Decide default evidence retention per compliance tier (45d vs 365d) and make it configurable in install manifest.
- Define exact severity mapping from RBAC denial reason codes to SIEM severity.

References & quick links:
- internal: confluence://INFRA-Private/mTLS-Gateway-Design
- infra repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/891
- JIRA: JIRA-PLAT-3421 (evidence export pipeline)

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally terse — expand into full runbook with scripts and terraform snippets if customer requests E2E validation during install.

-- Maya
